title: CDN as a Cache
description: Understand edge POP architecture, Cache-Control header semantics, cache key design, purge propagation, and how Cloudflare and Fastly architect their global cache networks.

segments.text: A CDN is the world's largest distributed cache. Cloudflare has over 300 edge locations. Fastly has about 90 POPs but with much higher capacity per POP. Understanding how CDN caching works lets you serve static and dynamic content with sub-50ms latency globally, offloading 90 percent or more of origin traffic.

A Point of Presence, or POP, is a data center at the network edge. When a user in Tokyo requests your content, the DNS routes them to the nearest POP. If the content is cached there, it's served in under 10 milliseconds. On a cache miss, the POP fetches from your origin server, caches the response, and serves future requests locally.

Cache-Control headers are your primary tool. max-age sets how long the edge caches content. s-maxage overrides max-age specifically for shared caches like CDNs while letting browsers use a different TTL. stale-while-revalidate serves stale content while fetching fresh content in the background. This eliminates cache stampedes.

stale-while-revalidate is the most underused header. Set Cache-Control to max-age 60 stale-while-revalidate 300. For the first 60 seconds, content is fresh. From 60 to 360 seconds, the CDN serves stale content instantly while fetching fresh content asynchronously. Users never wait for origin. This pattern eliminates latency spikes on cache expiry.

The cache key determines what's considered the same content. By default, it's the full URL including query parameters. Problem: URLs with tracking parameters like utm_source create duplicate cache entries for identical content. Cloudflare lets you customize cache keys to ignore specific query parameters, saving cache space and improving hit rates.
segments.thought_prompt: If your API returns different content based on Accept-Language header, how should you configure the cache key?

segments.text: The Vary header tells the CDN which request headers affect the response. Vary: Accept-Encoding caches separate copies for gzip and brotli. Vary: Accept-Language caches per language. But be careful: Vary: Cookie effectively disables caching because every user has different cookies. Use Vary surgically or your cache hit rate drops to near zero.

When you update content, you need to invalidate the cache. CDN purge propagation takes 1 to 30 seconds depending on the provider. Fastly does instant purge in under 150 milliseconds globally using a distributed purge protocol. Cloudflare takes up to 30 seconds. For time-sensitive content like stock prices, this latency difference matters.

Without origin shield, every POP that has a cache miss hits your origin. With 300 POPs and a cache miss storm, your origin sees 300 simultaneous requests for the same content. Origin shield designates a single POP as the intermediate cache. All other POPs fetch from the shield, and only the shield fetches from origin. This collapses 300 requests into one.

Modern CDNs run code at the edge. Cloudflare Workers, Fastly Compute@Edge, and AWS Lambda@Edge execute your code in the POP itself. You can personalize cached content, run A/B tests, rewrite headers, or authenticate requests without hitting origin. Shopify moved their storefront rendering to Cloudflare Workers, cutting p50 latency from 800 to 200 milliseconds.

You can cache dynamic content too. API responses with predictable TTLs, user-agnostic pages, search results for common queries. The key is identifying content that changes infrequently relative to how often it's requested. Even a 5-second cache on a high-traffic API endpoint can reduce origin load by 90 percent.

A real scenario: your e-commerce site launches a flash sale. Traffic spikes 50x. Your origin can handle 1,000 requests per second normally. Without CDN caching, origin dies immediately. With aggressive caching and stale-while-revalidate, the CDN absorbs the spike while origin updates content at its normal pace.
segments.thought_prompt: How would you configure CDN caching for a flash sale page that updates inventory every 10 seconds?

segments.text: A CDN is not just for static assets. It's a globally distributed cache that can absorb traffic spikes, reduce origin load by 90 percent, and serve content in under 50 milliseconds worldwide. Master Cache-Control headers, design your cache keys carefully, enable origin shield, and use stale-while-revalidate to eliminate latency spikes.
